[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/75/MY_Bob_Barker_at_Circular_Quay_Sydney.jpg/250px-MY_Bob_Barker_at_Circular_Quay_Sydney.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:MY_Bob_Barker_at_Circular_Quay_Sydney.jpg)

[MY _Bob Barker_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MY_Bob_Barker "MY Bob Barker") berthed at [Circular Quay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circular_Quay "Circular Quay") in [Sydney, Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney "Sydney"), in 2012

Sea Shepherd refer to the ships it has operated as [Neptune's Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neptune's_Navy "Neptune's Navy"). As of 2021[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society&action=edit), the conservation society operates 12 ships: _Ocean Warrior_, _Brigitte Bardot_, _Bob Barker_, _Steve Irwin_, _Sam Simon_, _John Paul DeJoria_, _Farley Mowat_, _Sharpie_, _Jairo Mora Sandoval_, _White Holly_, _Martin Sheen_ and _Sea Eagle_.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-70)

The _Steve Irwin_ was obtained in 2007 and originally called the _Robert Hunter_, named in honor of [Robert Hunter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Hunter_(journalist) "Robert Hunter (journalist)"),[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-71) co-founder of [Greenpeace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenpeace "Greenpeace").[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-Herald_Sun_2007-12-05-72) Irwin's widow, [Terri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terri_Irwin "Terri Irwin"), gave her support to Sea Shepherd, saying: "Whales have always been in Steve's heart and in 2006 he was investigating the possibility of joining the Sea Shepherd on part of its journey to defend these beautiful animals."[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-Shipping_Times_2007-12-06-73) The other ship, the 1200 ton _Bob Barker_, was named after well-known television game show host and animal activist [Bob Barker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Barker "Bob Barker"), who made the purchase in [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana") of the retired Norwegian whaling vessel possible with a donation of US$5 million.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-74) In February 2010, the _Bob Barker_ collided with the Japanese whaling vessel _Yushin Maru No. 3_, tearing a gash in the hull of the _Bob Barker_.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-75) In December 2014, the Bob Barker began its pursuit of the [illegal fishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illegal_fishing "Illegal fishing") vessel, the [FV _Thunder_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FV_Thunder "FV Thunder"), part of the [Bandit 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandit_6 "Bandit 6") and involved in [illegally fishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illegal,_unreported_and_unregulated_fishing "Illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing") the [Patagonian toothfish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patagonian_toothfish "Patagonian toothfish"), which became the longest chase in nautical history covering over 10,000 nautical miles and lasting 110 days.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-76)

The group also formerly operated the _[Farley Mowat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RV\_Farley\_Mowat "RV Farley Mowat")_ (impounded by the Canadian government, with Sea Shepherd having stated that they have no intention of paying the legal fines and berthage fees to recover their now obsolete vessel) and the _Ady Gil_, formerly known as the _Earthrace_ (sunk after a collision with the [MV _Shōnan Maru 2_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MV_Sh%C5%8Dnan_Maru_2 "MV Shōnan Maru 2") whaling security vessel in early 2010)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-whalewars1-77) as well as a number of earlier vessels.

Sea Shepherd acquired the _Ocean 7 Adventurer_ for its 2010/11 campaign against Japanese whaling in the Antarctic.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-78) In November 2010, Mayor [Brad Pettitt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pettitt "Brad Pettitt") of [Fremantle, Western Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fremantle,_Western_Australia "Fremantle, Western Australia"), christened the vessel _Gojira_ with Fremantle as its home port, making this the first Sea Shepherd ship registered in Australia, with an Australian crew. The _Gojira_ was renamed [MV _Brigitte Bardot_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MV_Brigitte_Bardot "MV Brigitte Bardot") in May 2011 after complaints of [copyright infringement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copyright_infringement "Copyright infringement") by [Toho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toho "Toho").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-79)

For the 2011–2012 [Antarctic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antarctic "Antarctic") campaign, the organization acquired [drone aircraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unmanned_aerial_vehicle "Unmanned aerial vehicle") to assist in their surveillance of the whaling ships.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-80)

In July 2012, [Sam Simon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Simon "Sam Simon"), a co-creator of _[The Simpsons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Simpsons "The Simpsons")_, reportedly donated money to purchase the fourth vessel, a former German [icebreaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Icebreaker "Icebreaker").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-81) The actual ship however turned out to be a former Japanese weather survey vessel, now called the MY _Sam Simon_.

On October 18, 2014, the actor [Martin Sheen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Sheen "Martin Sheen") unveiled Sea Shepherd's newest vessel, R/V _Martin Sheen_, named in his honor,[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-82) and captained by Oona Layolle of France. The name of this vessel carries the [prefix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship_identifier "Ship identifier") "R/V" because it will be engaged in direct action as a research vessel.

In January 2015, two decommissioned, 30-knot, [Island-class Coast Guard cutters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island-class_patrol_boat "Island-class patrol boat") were spotted flying the Sea Shepherd flag in Annapolis Yacht Basin.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-83) In June 2015, Sea Shepherd revealed on their website that they had purchased these vessels.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-84) One is named [MY _Farley Mowat_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MY_Farley_Mowat "MY Farley Mowat"), after an earlier vessel impounded by the Canadian government, and the other was named MY _Jules Verne_, after the author of the 1870 novel _[Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty\_Thousand\_Leagues\_Under\_the\_Seas "Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas")_, but was renamed [MV _John Paul DeJoria_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MV_John_Paul_DeJoria "MV John Paul DeJoria") on January 31, 2017.

On December 7, 2017, the organization announced the acquisition of a third [Island-class Cutter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island-class_patrol_boat "Island-class patrol boat") thanks to a donation from Chris Sharp, a biotech businessman. The vessel was named [MV _Sharpie_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MV_Sharpie "MV Sharpie"), and for its maiden mission it will join [Operation Milagro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society_operations#Operation_Milagro_(2015%E2%80%93present) "Sea Shepherd Conservation Society operations") in the Gulf of California to help save the endangered [vaquita porpoise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaquita "Vaquita").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-85)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-86)

The ships of the fleet have [flown the flags](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maritime_flag "Maritime flag") of a variety of different nations.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-NORSK-87)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-Mohawk_Traditional_Council_2009-02-13-88)[Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada"), [Belize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belize "Belize"), [UK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom") and [Togo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Togo "Togo") have [revoked the registrations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship_registration "Ship registration") of various vessels.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-OKADA-89)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-The_Sydney_Morning_Herald_2007-01-06-90)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-theage-91) Both the _[Steve Irwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MY\_Steve\_Irwin "MY Steve Irwin")_ and _[Bob Barker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MY\_Bob\_Barker "MY Bob Barker")_ ships now sail under Dutch flag leading to direct complaints by the Japanese government towards Dutch ambassadors. [The Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands") consequently considered revoking the registrations for both vessels but finally decided not to do so.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-92)

## Government response

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/04/MV_Steve_Irwin_Melbourne.jpg/250px-MV_Steve_Irwin_Melbourne.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:MV_Steve_Irwin_Melbourne.jpg)

[MY _Steve Irwin_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MY_Steve_Irwin "MY Steve Irwin") approaching [Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne "Melbourne"), [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_(Australia) "Victoria (Australia)")

In testimony on "[The Threat of Eco-Terrorism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Scare "Green Scare")" given to a US congressional subcommittee in 2002, Sea Shepherd was the first group mentioned by an FBI official for having attacked [commercial fishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commercial_fishing "Commercial fishing") operations by cutting [drift nets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drift_netting "Drift netting").[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-fbi-93) An earlier Canadian intelligence report on "[single issue terrorism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single_issue_terrorism "Single issue terrorism")" stated that "Watson and his supporters have been involved in a number of militant actions against whale hunting, driftnet fishing, seal hunting and other related issues" and mentions "activities against logging operations in Canada".[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-csis-94) In 2007, [Ian Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Campbell_(Australian_politician) "Ian Campbell (Australian politician)"), then the [Australian Environment Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_for_Sustainability,_Environment,_Water,_Population_and_Communities_(Australia) "Minister for Sustainability, Environment, Water, Population and Communities (Australia)") and a vigorous critic of Japan's whaling, once opposed Sea Shepherd's tactics, saying that it really put the cause of conservation backwards.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-TimesOnline-95) Due to the 2008 operations against Canadian seal hunters, [Danny Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Williams_(Canadian_politician) "Danny Williams (Canadian politician)"), [Premier of Newfoundland and Labrador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_of_Newfoundland_and_Labrador "Premier of Newfoundland and Labrador"), called Watson a terrorist and said that Sea Shepherd was not welcome in the province.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-CTV.ca_2008-04-14-96) The group has been accused of [eco-terrorism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eco-terrorism "Eco-terrorism") by the Japanese government,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-Telegraph_2009-04-17-4) whose internationally banned [whaling program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whaling_in_Japan "Whaling in Japan")[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-:0-97) is a principal focus of the Sea Shepherd. It has also been opposed by some countries that also oppose whaling, including Australia and New Zealand.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-TimesOnline-95)

Sea Shepherd has based many of its operations out of Australia with foreign crew members being able to travel in and out of the country on tourist [visas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visa_(document) "Visa (document)"),[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-visa-98) but in October 2009, the Australian Immigration Department imposed additional criminal background checks on Watson and his first officer, Peter Hammarstedt, when they applied for visas. Watson criticized the action as a submission to Japanese pressure by the [Rudd government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudd_Government_(2007%E2%80%9310) "Rudd Government (2007–10)").[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-visa-98) The Australian government rejected the idea it had delayed the visas, and on October 20, 2009, they were issued.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-99) By contrast, the [Tasmanian Greens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasmanian_Greens "Tasmanian Greens") and the former Greens Senator [Bob Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Brown "Bob Brown"), has endorsed and supported Sea Shepherd in various ways, including through advocacy within the Australian government and public endorsement of the group.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-100) However, when the _Steve Irwin_ returned to [Hobart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hobart "Hobart"), [Tasmania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasmania "Tasmania"), in February 2009, Australian Federal Police seized film footage and the ship's logs, reportedly prompted by complaints from Japan.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-101)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-102) Brown demanded that the Australian Prime Minister, [Kevin Rudd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Rudd "Kevin Rudd"), order their immediate return, but a spokesman for the Home Affairs Minister said it was a federal police matter.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-103) In 2013, [Julie Bishop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julie_Bishop "Julie Bishop"), the Foreign Minister of Australia, told the press club of Japan, "We do not, and will never, condone reckless, dangerous, unlawful behaviour. And where it occurs on the high seas, we will unreservedly condemn it. The fact that the Sea Shepherd visits Australian ports or some of the Sea Shepherd fleet might be registered in Australia is not indicative in any way of the Australian government's support for the organisation."[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-104) When Sea Shepherd indicated it was abandoning pursuit of Japanese whalers in 2017, Watson noted the hostility of the governments in the US, Australia and [New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand "New Zealand"), which he accused of acting "in league with Japan" against the organisation.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-Pursuit2018-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-cnn.com-50)

Officials in Japan have attempted to combat Sea Shepherd at the highest levels, discussing the revocation of the group's [tax exempt status](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/501(c)_organization "501(c) organization") with their counterparts in the United States.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-HP20110103-105)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-TA20110104-106)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-WSJ20110103-107) In December 2011, the [Institute of Cetacean Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institute_of_Cetacean_Research "Institute of Cetacean Research") (ICR) and [Kyodo Senpaku](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyodo_Senpaku "Kyodo Senpaku") Kaisha, the two Japanese organizations which operate Japan's whaling program, requested an [injunction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Injunction "Injunction") in the [US district court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_district_court "US district court") in [Seattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle "Seattle") to stop Sea Shepherd's operations against Japanese whalers.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-108) The federal court denied the ICR's preliminary injunction against SSCS.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-109) The ICR and Kyodo Senpaku appealed and, on December 17, 2012, the [United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Court_of_Appeals_for_the_Ninth_Circuit "United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit") issued an injunction against Paul Watson and Sea Shepherd and requiring them to stay at least 500 yd (457 m) from ICR vessels.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-110)[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-defiance-111) After the court ruling, Paul Watson stepped down and [Bob Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Brown "Bob Brown") succeeded as the leader of Sea Shepherd,[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-112)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-113) which launched an ultimately rejected appeal to have the injunction set aside.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-114) On the appeal's conclusion, the [Court of Appeals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appellate_court "Appellate court") stated that SSCS's activities were "the very embodiment of [piracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piracy_in_the_21st_century "Piracy in the 21st century")".[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-115)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-116) This reversed a previous decision by [Richard A. Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_A._Jones "Richard A. Jones"), who was removed as trial judge for abuse of discretion.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-117)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-118) As a result, [Paul Watson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Watson "Paul Watson") and US members of Sea Shepherd are currently prohibited by US courts from approaching Japanese whalers, even if they are observed acting in defiance of [international law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_law "International law"), including by killing whales in protected waters.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-defiance-111)

In March 2012, reacting to Paul Watson's allegation that [Maltese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malta "Malta") politicians were bribed by the [bluefin tuna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bluefin_tuna "Bluefin tuna") industry, Prime Minister of Malta [Lawrence Gonzi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Gonzi "Lawrence Gonzi") announced that the government would initiate [libel proceedings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defamation "Defamation") against the Sea Shepherd founder.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-119)

In May 2012, Watson was detained by German authorities after he arrived at the Frankfurt Airport based on a request from the government of [Costa Rica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costa_Rica "Costa Rica") on the charge of violating navigational regulations.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-120) The charge stemmed from an altercation in 2002 took place during filming for the documentary _[Sharkwater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharkwater "Sharkwater"),_[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-121) in which Sea Shepherd contended that the other vessel was [shark finning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shark_finning "Shark finning") in [Guatemalan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guatemala "Guatemala") waters.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-122) Watson subsequently [skipped bail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bail "Bail") and went into hiding.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-123) The Costa Rican government subsequently requested the [Interpol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Criminal_Police_Organization "International Criminal Police Organization") to issue a [Red Notice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpol_notice#Notice_types "Interpol notice") arrest request for Watson to its member countries.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-124)

Watson said on the [Discovery Channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discovery_Channel "Discovery Channel") in 2009 that the [Dalai Lama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalai_Lama "Dalai Lama") had sent a letter of support for Sea Shepherd's volunteers accompanied by a wrathful, scowling statue of the deity [Hayagriva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayagriva "Hayagriva"), which expresses compassion and determination in overcoming obstacles.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-Telegraph_2009-04-17-4) However, during a visit to Japan in 2010, the Dalai Lama said that while he agrees with the goal of stopping Japan from hunting whales, they should stop using violent methods to achieve that goal.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_Shepherd_Conservation_Society#cite_note-AFP20100619-125)
